paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar ben Yirmeyah, [Sotah 4a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.4a.3). Kahana bar Yirmeyah, Orlah ch. 3, halakhah 2.
Rabbi Meyisha son of Rabbi Yirmeyah, Yerushalmi, end of Nazir. Menashya bar Yirmeyah, [Pesachim 68a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.68a.11).

Rav Sama son of Rav Yirmeyah, [Ketubot 33a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.33a.7).[^3] Rava bar Yirmeyah, [Berakhot 43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.43a.13). Rabbah bar Yirmeyah, [Pesachim 36a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.36a.14).[^2]

notes.text: The notice leaves the source of the Orlah chapter/halakhah reference unspecified; it is not automatically labeled Jerusalem Talmud or Tosefta. Rava and Rabbah remain separate spellings.

Berakhot gives Rava as the person Rabbi Zeira quotes, while Pesachim 36a has Rabbah transmitting in Shmuel’s name through Rabbi Zeira’s report. The notice’s patronymics are drawn from separate passages.
Rav Sama son of Rav Yirmeyah asks whether conspiring witnesses require forewarning in this case. The answer appeals to the rule that the law should apply equally to all.
